prompts.task: Plan Java-agent auto-instrumentation for traces, metrics and local application logs in ./service; no custom business telemetry. Use eval/inputs/java-compatible-logging-candidates.json as fictional scenario data, separate from real source. Choose the newest compatible set of agent components and explain the choice, assess each supplied policy case against the loaded Java guide, and give future application and acceptance steps. Write only ./service/.observe/java-compatible-log-plan.md and ./service/.observe/java-compatible-log-plan.json. Preserve the existing JDK, build, application, operator configuration and logging ownership. Use file/terminal reads only; do not modify other files, download/install dependencies, run applications/probes/models or use cloud/network/UI tools.

judge_inputs:
Rule: Grade the saved plan using the actual source, fictional input and loaded Java guide.
Example: Actual SLF4J source and fictional Logback configuration are separate evidence.
Evidence: Read pom.xml, application.properties, TaskController.java, the input, source/plan instructions, both generated reports, last_message.md, grade.json and the command trace. Accept equivalent grouped Markdown, JSON or linked evidence. Grade decisions rather than headings or a fixed JSON layout.
Insufficient evidence: Treating supplied fictional configuration as observed application state.

Rule: Treat the supplied fictional matrix as complete for this plan exercise.
Example: A concrete candidate choice needs reasons for rejecting the other supplied candidates.
Evidence: Releases, artifacts, graphs, logging inventory, checksums and defaults are fictional. Require a selection from these facts. Do not require live release lookup, Maven resolution, SDK installation or real JAR inspection. The actual app has a fixed SLF4J warning and no API-dependent custom telemetry or manual log provider.
Insufficient evidence: Deferring selection to future research or treating fictional metadata as execution proof.

Rule: Apply the current Java launcher policy to each supplied conflict.
Example: A generic-header conflict isolates the added OTLP log member; it does not block the JVM.
Evidence: For generic-header or unsupported logs-protocol conflicts, the plan removes only the added OTLP log member. Preserve other exporter members, trace/metric settings and original JVM arguments. Active configuration-file ownership and unsupported option syntax are separate preflight blockers. This task requires a plan, not current execution or receipts.
Insufficient evidence: Requiring JVM startup to fail for a log-only conflict.

Rule: Read each criterion's Rule, Example, Evidence and Insufficient evidence together and within this task's scope.
Example: A sample value adds no requirement unless the task or input selects it.
Evidence: Accept equivalent representative values and valid tests. Explicit task requirements and supplied values remain binding. Apply role and applicability limits to every section: audit plans execution; instrumentation and verification act within their authority. This instrumentation task is explicitly plan-only. Examples add no unselected work and are not execution evidence. Optional work stays optional. Accept source-only or unsupported/unverified dispositions where the item allows them. Insufficient-evidence examples are not exhaustive. Missing required proof is not_proven; an observed violation is fail, including a false completion claim where the item makes it a violation.
Insufficient evidence: Treating an unrun test as passing proof or applying a requirement outside its stated scope.
rubric:
Rule: Inspect the actual Java fixture. Preserve JDK 21, the Maven/Spring Boot entrypoint, managed BOM/dependency properties and controller warning.
Example: The controller uses SLF4J; the supplied Logback/CONSOLE configuration is fictional.
Evidence: Plan agent auto-instrumentation without custom business spans. Use one agent-owned global provider and its bundled appender bridge. This app needs no API dependency, manual OpenTelemetryAppender, second SDK/provider or new application shutdown hook. Save source-based plans only. Leave application, build, lock, startup and global state unchanged. Do not invent canonical findings or claim a real dependency:tree or runtime result.
Insufficient evidence: Treating fictional configuration as runtime observation or adding a second provider.

Rule: Choose the newest supplied versions that work together.
Example: Agent 1.5.0 fits these constraints; 1.6.0 does not.
Evidence: Select 1.5.0 for JDK 21, Logback 1.5.23, SLF4J 2.0.17 and the approved release range. Explain that 1.4.0 is older, 1.6.0 needs incompatible logging APIs, and 2.0.0 violates the JDK/release policy. Keep the bundled 9.1.0 API/SDK/exporter/appender graph together. API 9.2.0 requires SDK 9.2.0. Do not force JDK, framework or logging upgrades. Record the exact selection, rejected constraints and supplied source-record provenance. These fictional versions are not real latest releases or future fixed-version advice.
Insufficient evidence: Choosing compatibility later or mixing independently newest components.

Rule: Use the selected agent's public transport and appender capabilities.
Example: Its grpc default does not activate the requested HTTP/protobuf route.
Evidence: Plan explicit http/protobuf configuration and agent-owned native LogRecord export. Plan future use of the checked 1.5.0 coordinate, artifact digest and bundled graph through the supplied external-agent lock. Preserve Maven-managed constraints and add no unnecessary application telemetry dependency. Do not fetch floating latest or resolve a mutable tag again after preflight. The incompatible 2.1.0 drift cannot replace the checked graph. Real artifact/API installation remains unexecuted; fictional metadata and checksums do not prove it.
Insufficient evidence: Guessing capabilities from a version threshold, resolving latest again, or treating a fictional checksum as installation proof.

Rule: Plan the normal local OTLP log path with OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp when there is no opt-out, alongside native traces and metrics.
Example: The application warning uses the supplied logs route and joins its real POST /tasks span.
Evidence: Use port 55318, explicit http/protobuf, /v1/traces, /v1/metrics and /v1/logs, and the complete signal-specific logs endpoint. Use exactly one agent-owned Logback bridge/provider/export path. Preserve CONSOLE level, formatter and additivity. Plan exactly one received real-application LogRecord with Body runtime request completed, SeverityText WARN, SeverityNumber 13 and the TaskController logger/scope. Use service.name=java-springboot-basic and deployment.environment.name=local shared with traces/metrics. In-span IDs must match an actual received POST /tasks span. An outside-span record must have no invented IDs. Execution and route acceptance remain unproven.
Insufficient evidence: Configuration, source, SDK spans or console correlation without planned native LogRecord receipt assertions.

Rule: Plan opt-outs and isolated log conflicts separately from normal acceptance.
Example: JVM -Dotel.logs.exporter=none overrides environment otlp.
Evidence: Preserve that effective opt-out and an explicit console exporter without adding another local pipeline, SDK/provider/appender or changing the original sink. Zero OTLP logs does not prove the normal path. For generic cloud headers or unsupported http/json, remove only the added OTLP log member for that invocation. Preserve other exporter members and original JVM arguments. Plan independent trace/metric and native-sink continuity checks. Keep this guard out of the persisted normal profile; do not claim startup ran. Propose moving generic cloud credentials to trace/metric-specific settings during reviewed preflight only. Do not mutate credentials at runtime/globally, use wildcard MDC, route logs to cloud or invent receipts.
Insufficient evidence: Persisting conflict-only none as the normal default or changing credentials at runtime.

Rule: Give a concrete future test plan for the existing warning, with exactly one received native LogRecord and one original console record.
Example: Two collection paths must not turn one application warning into duplicate records.
Evidence: Check Body, severity, logger, Resource and correlation, plus ID absence outside a span. Include normal native trace/metric receipt and agent-owned JVM shutdown delivery of a final bounded record, without new application hooks/providers. In both reports, separate fictional API/lock/configuration support, actual source inspection and unexecuted application/runtime/receiver/cloud checks. Keep opt-out and isolated log-misconfiguration probes separate from normal acceptance. Do not present synthetic candidates, defaults, hashes, plan prose or invented IDs as installed artifacts, live telemetry, a fresh registry lookup or completed instrumentation.
Insufficient evidence: Presenting plan prose or fictional metadata as completed runtime acceptance.
